name: relative-frequency
title: Relative frequency (experimental vs theoretical)
tagline: Experimental relative-frequency line settling toward an amber theoretical level; derives RF at each milestone and expected frequency; fair vs biased.
description: A line graph of experimental relative frequency (0–1, up the side) against the number of trials (along the bottom), settling toward a theoretical probability drawn as a horizontal amber reference line — the model for relative frequency, experimental vs theoretical probability, fairness and expected frequency. You give each series its trial data as cumulative counts at a list of trial milestones (e.g. 2 sixes after 10 throws, 14 after 100, 99 after 600) and, optionally, the theoretical probability as a fraction (1/6); the model derives the relative frequency at every milestone (count ÷ trials), the joining line, the markers, the theoretical line and its label, and the expected frequency (P × number of trials). Plot two or three series on the same axes to compare a fair experiment converging to its theoretical value against a biased one converging somewhere else. Occlude a theoretical line to ask "what does it settle on?". Make it draggable so pupils sweep the number of trials and watch the relative frequency settle.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever experimental probability is taught by watching the relative frequency of an event settle as the number of trials grows: relative frequency tables and graphs ("after 10, 50, 100, … throws"), experimental vs theoretical probability, deciding whether a coin / die / spinner is fair or biased, and expected frequency. Author the experiment, never the curve: each series carries data as a list of { n, count } where n is a number-of-trials milestone and count is the cumulative number of times the tracked event has happened in the first n trials — the model plots (n, count ÷ n) and joins the points. Give the known probability as theoretical: { num, den } (a fraction such as 1/6, 1/2, 3/10); it is drawn as a horizontal dashed amber line at that height and labelled with the fraction — the value the experiment should converge to. Common configurations: a single fair experiment converging to its theoretical line (the worked example); a fair vs biased comparison — two series, two theoretical lines, settling at different heights (give each a label so the legend names them); an answer space — a series with empty data on labelled axes for pupils to plot from their own table; an estimate question — show the settling line but set theoretical.occlude so its value reads "?" ("estimate the probability"); expected frequency — set showExpected to print "P × n = expected (got observed)" for each series. Keep yMax low (e.g. 0.4) to zoom in on a small probability like 1/6, or leave it at 1 for a coin. Keep the same axes across a lesson so pupils compare like with like. A staged build reads very well: open on the axes with the theoretical line drawn, then reveal the experimental line over a few stages (volatile at first, then settling) and bring in the expected-frequency readout last — the base (labelled axes + target line) stands alone. Set draggable for a web slider that sweeps the number of trials and grows the line so pupils see it settle. Switch model when the teaching is not convergence-over-trials: for a one-off distribution of outcomes (frequency per category) use statistics/bar-chart; for sample-space counting use statistics/sample-space-grid; for a probability of compound events use probability/tree or probability/venn. Synonyms a teacher might use: relative frequency, experimental probability, estimated probability, experimental vs theoretical, fair, fairness, biased, bias, expected frequency, expected number, long-run proportion, convergence, settles down, law of large numbers.

series.description: The experimental series — one line each. Most figures have one; give two or three (each with a label) to compare a fair experiment against a biased one on shared axes. Each series's colour is assigned automatically from the categorical palette (blue, then teal, then purple) — never amber, which is reserved for the theoretical line.

label.description: The trace's name, shown in the legend when there are two or more series and used in the description, e.g. "Fair die — P(six)" or "Biased spinner". Omit for a single unlabelled line.

data.description: The experiment as cumulative readings: one { n, count } per trial milestone. The relative frequency at each milestone is DERIVED as count ÷ n and the points are joined into the line. Order does not matter (points are sorted by n). Give an EMPTY array for an answer space — labelled axes with no line for pupils to plot themselves.

n.description: A number-of-trials milestone (the x value), e.g. 10, 50, 100, 600.

count.description: The CUMULATIVE number of times the tracked event happened in the first n trials (not the count in this batch alone). Relative frequency = count ÷ n; a count above n is clamped to n.

theoretical.description: The known (theoretical) probability the experiment should converge to, as a fraction — drawn as a horizontal dashed amber line at height num ÷ den and labelled with the fraction. Omit when the theoretical value is unknown (a pure "where does it settle?" investigation).

num.description: Numerator of the probability fraction, e.g. 1 in 1/6.

den.description: Denominator of the probability fraction, e.g. 6 in 1/6.

occlude.description: Render the theoretical line's value as "?" instead of the fraction — the line still shows where it settles, the question asks pupils to name the probability. Default false.

axes.description: The window and axis titles. Keep these identical across the blocks of one lesson so pupils compare like with like.

yMax.description: Top of the relative-frequency axis (which always starts at 0). Default 1. Lower it to zoom in on a small probability — e.g. 0.4 makes the convergence to 1/6 easy to read.

xMax.description: Top of the number-of-trials axis. Default: just beyond the largest milestone in the data.

xStep.description: Gap between x gridlines / axis numbers. Default: a sensible round value.

yStep.description: Gap between y gridlines / axis numbers. Default: a sensible round value.

xLabel.description: The x-axis title. Default "Number of trials". Keep it short — a long title is shrunk to fit.

yLabel.description: The y-axis title. Default "Relative frequency". Keep it short (it runs up the side); "Relative frequency of a six" is about the longest that reads well.

grid.description: Show the background grid (helps read values off the axes). Default true.

markers.description: Draw a dot at each plotted reading (each row of the table). Default true; turn off for a very dense line.

showExpected.description: Print an expected-frequency readout for each series with a (non-occluded) theoretical line: "P × n = expected (got observed)", using the largest milestone as n. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

draggable.description: Web-only. Adds a "trials" slider below the plot: pupils sweep the number of trials and the experimental line grows to that point, with a live readout of the current n and relative frequency — so they watch it settle toward the theoretical line. The static figure already shows the whole line. Default false.
